title: Fuel Temperature Sensor A Circuit Low
shortDescription: The fuel temperature sensor A circuit is reporting a voltage below the expected range.
fullDescription:
P0182 indicates the ECM has detected the fuel temperature sensor A signal is lower than the calibrated minimum threshold. This sensor measures fuel temperature to adjust fuel delivery and density compensation.

A low voltage often means a short to ground in the sensor or wiring, or a failed sensor element. Incorrect fuel temperature readings can cause poor fuel economy and drivability issues.
safetyImpact: Low driveability impact, but may affect cold-start or flex-fuel adjustments.

causes.cause: Short to ground in signal wire

fixSteps.title: Scan codes
fixSteps.instruction: Retrieve all DTCs and freeze frame data.

fixSteps.title: Inspect sensor wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Check connector and wiring for shorts to ground.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Replace fuel temperature sensor if resistance is out of spec.

faq.a: Short distances are fine, but address it to avoid fuel economy and emissions issues.

title: Fuel Temperature Sensor A Circuit High
shortDescription: The fuel temperature sensor A signal voltage is above the expected range.
fullDescription:
P0183 sets when the ECM reads fuel temperature sensor voltage above threshold, indicating open circuit or short to voltage.

The engine may default to a fixed fuel temperature value, causing fuel metering inaccuracies, especially in flex-fuel vehicles.

fixSteps.title: Check connector
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect the sensor connector for damage.

fixSteps.title: Measure resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Compare sensor resistance to spec at temperature.

faq.a: Usually a small two-wire sensor in the fuel rail or fuel tank.

title: Fuel Temperature Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
shortDescription: Fuel temperature sensor A signal is intermittent or erratic.
fullDescription:
P0184 indicates the ECM detected an unstable signal from the fuel temperature sensor. The value jumps outside acceptable limits over short periods.

This is commonly due to loose connectors, chafed wiring, or a failing sensor.
safetyImpact: Minor but can cause inconsistent fueling.

fixSteps.title: Wiggle test
fixSteps.instruction: Wiggle connectors and wiring while monitoring live data.

fixSteps.title: Repair wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Re-pin or replace damaged connector sections.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Swap sensor if wiring is good.

faq.a: They require catching the fault while it's happening, often via wiggle tests.

title: Fuel Temperature Sensor B Circuit Malfunction
shortDescription: The second fuel temperature sensor circuit has a malfunction.
fullDescription:
P0185 is set when the secondary fuel temperature sensor (sensor B) circuit is malfunctioning. Some vehicles use two sensors for rail and tank fuel temperature.

The ECM uses both values for density and trim calculations.

fixSteps.title: Identify sensor B location
fixSteps.instruction: Refer to vehicle service info for sensor B.

fixSteps.title: Test sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance and compare to chart.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new fuel temp sensor B.

faq.q: Does my car have sensor B?
faq.a: Not all vehicles. Check service documentation to confirm.

title: Fuel Temperature Sensor B Range/Performance
shortDescription: Fuel temperature sensor B signal is out of expected range.
fullDescription:
P0186 triggers when the ECM detects sensor B readings inconsistent with engine conditions (e.g., doesn't track coolant or ambient). The sensor may be stuck or biased.

It's often a prelude to a full sensor failure.

fixSteps.title: Read sensor data
fixSteps.instruction: Compare sensor B with sensor A and ambient temperature.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new sensor if readings are biased.

faq.a: The signal is electrically OK but the value is implausible.

title: Fuel Temperature Sensor B Circuit Low
shortDescription: Fuel temperature sensor B voltage is below threshold.
fullDescription:
P0187 sets when sensor B voltage is too low, typically from a short to ground or failed sensor. The ECM may substitute a default value.

Long-term fuel trim can drift slightly while the fault is active.

faq.q: Do I need a scan tool?
faq.a: Yes, to read freeze frame and verify the fault is cleared.

title: Fuel Temperature Sensor B Circuit High
shortDescription: Fuel temperature sensor B signal voltage is above threshold.
fullDescription:
P0188 indicates sensor B voltage is too high, suggesting an open circuit or short to voltage. The ECM substitutes a default value.

Ignoring it can cause slight fuel trim discrepancies over time.

fixSteps.title: Back-probe connector
fixSteps.instruction: Check for 5V reference and ground at sensor.

fixSteps.title: Repair wiring or replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Fix open circuit or install new sensor.

faq.a: Not usually, but fix it to prevent future fueling inaccuracies.

title: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Circuit Malfunction
shortDescription: The fuel rail pressure sensor circuit has a general malfunction.
fullDescription:
P0190 is set when the ECM detects an electrical fault with the fuel rail pressure sensor. On direct-injection and diesel engines, this sensor is critical for precise fuel delivery.

A malfunction can cause hard start, stalling, or limp mode.
safetyImpact: Possible stalling and limp mode; drive carefully.

fixSteps.title: Scan and review data
fixSteps.instruction: Check live fuel rail pressure and commanded pressure.

fixSteps.title: Test sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Check sensor reference, ground, and signal voltages.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Replace fuel rail pressure sensor following safe fuel procedures.

faq.a: Only with fuel system safety knowledge; high-pressure fuel systems are dangerous.

title: Engine Oil Temperature Sensor Low
shortDescription: Engine oil temperature sensor voltage is below the expected range.
fullDescription:
P0197 indicates a low voltage signal from the engine oil temperature sensor. The ECM uses oil temp for variable valve timing, oil pressure control, and cooling system decisions.

A low reading can cause incorrect VVT, mild performance issues, and inaccurate oil life monitoring.
safetyImpact: Low, but affects oil monitoring systems.

causes.cause: Short to ground in signal wire

fixSteps.title: Scan live data
fixSteps.instruction: Compare oil temperature to coolant temperature after warmup.

fixSteps.title: Test sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Measure sensor resistance against temperature chart.

faq.a: Not usually, but fix it to avoid VVT and oil monitoring issues.

title: Engine Oil Temperature Sensor High
shortDescription: Engine oil temperature sensor voltage is above the expected range.
fullDescription:
P0198 sets when the oil temperature sensor reports a voltage higher than the valid range. The circuit may be open or shorted to voltage.

The ECM typically substitutes a default value, which may affect variable valve timing and oil monitoring.

fixSteps.title: Inspect connector
fixSteps.instruction: Check for bent pins and corrosion.

fixSteps.title: Verify wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Check signal and ground circuits for continuity.

faq.q: Can I just reset the code?
faq.a: It will return if the circuit issue isn't fixed.

title: Injection Timing Control Circuit Malfunction
shortDescription: The injection timing control circuit has a fault affecting fuel injection timing.
fullDescription:
P0216 commonly applies to diesel and some older gasoline engines with mechanical/electronic injection timing controls. The ECM has detected an electrical or performance fault in the timing solenoid circuit.

Incorrect injection timing can cause power loss, smoke, excess emissions, and knock.
safetyImpact: Reduced power and potential engine damage under load.

fixSteps.title: Scan and inspect
fixSteps.instruction: Retrieve DTCs and review freeze frame data.

fixSteps.title: Test solenoid
fixSteps.instruction: Check resistance and actuation of timing solenoid.

fixSteps.title: Repair or replace
fixSteps.instruction: Replace solenoid or repair wiring as needed.

faq.a: Avoid heavy load; get it diagnosed promptly.

title: Engine Overtemperature Condition
shortDescription: The ECM has detected an engine overheating condition.
fullDescription:
P0217 sets when coolant temperature exceeds a critical threshold. It's often a symptom of cooling system failure — low coolant, stuck thermostat, bad water pump, or failed fan.

Continued operation can cause severe engine damage including warped heads and blown head gaskets.
safetyImpact: Immediate risk of engine damage; stop driving if overheating.

fixSteps.title: Stop and cool down
fixSteps.instruction: Park safely and let engine cool before inspecting.

fixSteps.title: Check coolant
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect coolant level and for leaks.

fixSteps.title: Test thermostat and fan
fixSteps.instruction: Verify thermostat opens and fan runs at temperature.

fixSteps.title: Repair root cause
fixSteps.instruction: Replace thermostat, fan, or water pump as required.

faq.a: No. Overheating can destroy the engine quickly.

title: Transmission Over Temperature Condition
shortDescription: The transmission fluid temperature exceeds safe operating limits.
fullDescription:
P0218 signals the transmission is overheating. It's typically triggered by low or old fluid, heavy towing, cooler blockage, or internal transmission problems.

Overheating accelerates wear on clutches and seals, risking expensive damage.
safetyImpact: Transmission may go into limp mode; risk of transmission damage.

fixSteps.title: Check fluid level and condition
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect ATF level and smell for burnt odor.

fixSteps.title: Service transmission
fixSteps.instruction: Flush fluid and repair root cause.

faq.a: Low fluid, towing beyond capacity, and blocked coolers.

title: Engine Overspeed Condition
shortDescription: The engine RPM has exceeded the maximum safe limit.
fullDescription:
P0219 sets when the ECM detects engine RPM above the preset redline. This can occur from missed downshifts, clutch slip, fuel injector sticking open, or throttle malfunction.

Overspeeding can cause valve float and serious internal damage.
safetyImpact: High; risk of engine damage and loss of control.

fixSteps.title: Review freeze frame
fixSteps.instruction: Note RPM and vehicle speed at fault.

faq.q: What to do right after it happens?
faq.a: Stop driving and inspect for engine damage before continuing.

title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit Malfunction
shortDescription: The throttle or pedal position sensor B circuit is malfunctioning.
fullDescription:
P0220 indicates the ECM detected a general malfunction with the B sensor used for throttle or accelerator pedal position. Many electronic throttle systems use dual sensors for redundancy.

The engine often defaults to reduced power/limp mode.

fixSteps.title: Verify sensor voltages
fixSteps.instruction: Compare sensor A and B signals at idle and WOT.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor or TB
fixSteps.instruction: Replace sensor or throttle body assembly as required.

faq.a: If one sensor fails, the other prevents unsafe throttle conditions.

title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor B Range/Performance
shortDescription: Sensor B signal is out of expected range or inconsistent with sensor A.
fullDescription:
P0221 sets when sensor B does not track sensor A within expected tolerance. It may be drifting, sticking, or electrically degraded.

The vehicle will likely enter reduced-power mode as a safety measure.

fixSteps.title: Compare sensor outputs
fixSteps.instruction: Check A vs B signal alignment.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor/throttle body
fixSteps.instruction: Install new assembly if problem persists.

faq.a: Sometimes, but relearning may be required after cleaning.

title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit Low
shortDescription: Sensor B voltage is below the minimum threshold.
fullDescription:
P0222 indicates the sensor B signal is too low. The ECM interprets this as an electrical fault or failed sensor.

Expect reduced-power mode until the fault is cleared.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor/TB
fixSteps.instruction: Install new sensor or throttle body.

faq.a: Yes, but with limited throttle response.

title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit High
shortDescription: Sensor B voltage is above the maximum threshold.
fullDescription:
P0223 sets when sensor B voltage exceeds the calibrated high limit. An open circuit or short to voltage is typical.

Limp mode usually activates.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor/TB
fixSteps.instruction: Install new sensor or throttle body assembly.

faq.q: Do I need to relearn throttle?
faq.a: Usually yes after replacing a throttle body.

title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor B Intermittent
shortDescription: Sensor B has an intermittent electrical fault.
fullDescription:
P0224 indicates the sensor B signal cuts out or spikes intermittently, commonly due to loose connectors or internal sensor wear.

Can cause unpredictable throttle response.
safetyImpact: Unpredictable throttle; potential brief power loss.

fixSteps.title: Wiggle test connector
fixSteps.instruction: Monitor live data while wiggling harness.

faq.q: Why is intermittent hardest to fix?
faq.a: You must catch the fault while it's active.

title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor C Circuit Malfunction
shortDescription: Sensor C circuit has a general fault.
fullDescription:
P0225 applies to vehicles with a third throttle or pedal position sensor. The ECM has detected a general electrical malfunction.

Reduced-power mode often activates.

faq.a: No, only some models with multi-sensor pedal assemblies.

title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor C Range/Performance
shortDescription: Sensor C signal out of expected range or inconsistent with A/B.
fullDescription:
P0226 triggers when sensor C disagrees with A or B sensor beyond tolerance. Often caused by drift, mechanical wear, or dirty throttle.

Vehicle may enter reduced-power mode.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new sensor if drift remains.

faq.q: Do I need to relearn after cleaning?
faq.a: Yes, most vehicles require an idle relearn.

title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor C Circuit Low
shortDescription: Sensor C signal voltage below threshold.
fullDescription:
P0227 indicates sensor C has a low voltage, typically from short to ground or failed sensor. The ECM may enter limp mode.

Inspect wiring first before replacing parts.

fixSteps.title: Test wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Measure signal for shorts to ground.

faq.q: Does this code always trigger limp mode?
faq.a: Usually, yes, for safety.

title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor C Circuit High
shortDescription: Sensor C signal voltage above threshold.
fullDescription:
P0228 sets when sensor C reports voltage higher than normal. Open circuit or short to voltage is likely.

Expect reduced throttle response.

fixSteps.title: Verify reference/ground
fixSteps.instruction: Back-probe connector for reference voltage and ground.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor/TB
fixSteps.instruction: Install new sensor or throttle assembly.

faq.q: Should I replace the whole pedal?
faq.a: Often the sensor is integrated into the pedal assembly.

title: IAT Sensor 1 Circuit Intermittent
shortDescription: Intake Air Temperature sensor 1 is reporting intermittent signals.
fullDescription:
P0114 sets when the ECM detects erratic readings from the IAT sensor. This often stems from loose connectors, damaged wiring, or a failing sensor element.

Intermittent IAT readings can slightly affect fuel trim and timing.

fixSteps.title: Wiggle test
fixSteps.instruction: Monitor live data while wiggling connector.

fixSteps.title: Clean/repair connector
fixSteps.instruction: Fix terminals and check for corrosion.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new IAT sensor if needed.

faq.a: Usually minor but worth fixing to maintain fuel economy.

title: Engine Coolant Temperature Circuit Malfunction
shortDescription: The coolant temperature sensor circuit has a general malfunction.
fullDescription:
P0115 is a generic code indicating the ECM has detected an issue with the engine coolant temperature (ECT) sensor circuit. The sensor provides critical data used for fuel delivery, ignition timing, and fan operation.

A bad ECT sensor can cause hard starts, rough running, poor fuel economy, and overheating.
safetyImpact: May cause overheating if fan logic is affected.

fixSteps.title: Scan data
fixSteps.instruction: Compare ECT reading to IAT at cold start.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new ECT sensor with proper coolant precautions.

faq.a: Yes, if the fan command logic relies on the bad reading.

title: Engine Coolant Temperature Range/Performance
shortDescription: ECT sensor reading is out of expected range during operation.
fullDescription:
P0116 triggers when the ECT reading doesn't track normal engine warmup behavior. For example, temperature not rising after extended running, or being too far off from ambient at cold start.

Common causes include stuck-open thermostat or a drifting sensor.
safetyImpact: Can affect cabin heat and fuel trims.

fixSteps.title: Warmup test
fixSteps.instruction: Monitor ECT rise from cold start.

faq.q: How to tell thermostat vs sensor?
faq.a: Log ECT warmup curve — a stuck-open thermostat prevents reaching operating temp.

title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 1 Circuit Intermittent
shortDescription: ECT sensor 1 has intermittent signal issues.
fullDescription:
P0119 indicates the ECM has detected intermittent fluctuations in the coolant temperature sensor signal. This is typically due to wiring or connector issues, though sometimes the sensor element itself is failing.

The ECM may use a substituted value during fault.

fixSteps.title: Wiggle test
fixSteps.instruction: Watch for data drops during wiggle.

fixSteps.title: Repair connector
fixSteps.instruction: Re-pin or solder connector as needed.

faq.q: Will clearing the code fix it?
faq.a: No, the underlying wiring or sensor issue must be repaired.

title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit Malfunction
shortDescription: Throttle/pedal position sensor A circuit has a general fault.
fullDescription:
P0120 is set when the ECM detects an issue with sensor A of the throttle or pedal position sensor system. On drive-by-wire systems, this may cause reduced-power mode.

On older cable-throttle systems it typically affects idle and shift strategy.

faq.a: Yes on many vehicles after replacing the throttle assembly.

title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
shortDescription: Sensor A has intermittent electrical issues.
fullDescription:
P0124 indicates the ECM has detected erratic signals from sensor A. Intermittent codes are often caused by wiring, connectors, or sensors that fail under heat or vibration.

Running behavior may be unpredictable.

fixSteps.title: Live data wiggle
fixSteps.instruction: Wiggle harness and watch sensor signal.

fixSteps.title: Repair wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Address any damaged wiring or connectors.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new sensor if issue persists.

faq.a: Often temperature or vibration triggers the fault.

title: Insufficient Coolant Temperature for Closed Loop
shortDescription: Engine hasn't reached temperature needed for closed-loop fuel control.
fullDescription:
P0125 sets when the engine takes too long to reach operating temperature, preventing the ECM from entering closed-loop fuel control. A stuck-open thermostat is the most common cause.

Side effects include poor fuel economy, high emissions, and poor heater performance.

fixSteps.title: Monitor warmup
fixSteps.instruction: Scan ECT from cold start to normal temp.

fixSteps.title: Replace thermostat
fixSteps.instruction: If stuck open, install new thermostat.

fixSteps.title: Replace ECT sensor
fixSteps.instruction: If sensor is drifting, replace it.

faq.a: Replace the thermostat.

title: Insufficient Coolant Temperature for Stable Operation
shortDescription: Coolant temperature is too low for stable engine operation.
fullDescription:
P0126 is set when the engine cannot maintain adequate coolant temperature for stable running. Similar causes to P0125 apply, plus a weak cooling system balance.

This impacts idle quality and emissions.

faq.q: Does a thermostat help fuel economy?
faq.a: Yes, by allowing closed-loop operation sooner.

title: Intake Air Temperature Too High
shortDescription: IAT sensor reports excessively high intake air temperature.
fullDescription:
P0127 is set when the IAT is above the calibrated limit. Possible causes include heat soak, failed sensor, or airflow issues that starve intake cooling.

High IAT retards timing, reducing power and economy.

fixSteps.title: Monitor IAT
fixSteps.instruction: Log IAT during cold start and driving.

faq.q: Can hot weather alone cause this?
faq.a: No — the threshold is above normal ambient.

title: Coolant Thermostat Below Regulating Temperature (v2)
shortDescription: Coolant temperature is below expected regulating range during normal operation.
fullDescription:
Alternate description of P0128: the ECM models the expected coolant temperature from airflow, load, and ambient, and expects it to reach a specific regulated temperature. When it doesn't, the code sets.

This is most often caused by a stuck or weak thermostat.
safetyImpact: Low but increases emissions and reduces fuel economy.

fixSteps.title: Log warmup
fixSteps.instruction: Monitor ECT reaching operating temp over 20 minutes of driving.

faq.a: Aftermarket thermostats may have wrong open temperatures.

title: Barometric Pressure Too Low
shortDescription: The barometric pressure sensor reports pressure below valid range.
fullDescription:
P0129 sets when the BARO sensor reports an implausibly low pressure. This can affect fuel and timing calculations.

It's usually caused by a failed sensor or wiring fault, not actual low atmospheric pressure.

fixSteps.title: Read sensor value
fixSteps.instruction: Compare scan tool BARO to known local ambient.

faq.a: No, this code refers to an out-of-range reading, not actual altitude.

title: O2 Sensor Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
shortDescription: The upstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 has a circuit malfunction.
fullDescription:
P0130 indicates the ECM has detected a general fault with the B1S1 oxygen sensor circuit. This upstream sensor is critical for fuel trim adjustments.

A faulty signal can cause poor fuel economy, elevated emissions, and possible catalytic converter damage over time.
safetyImpact: Moderate; long-term damage to catalyst possible.

fixSteps.title: Check live data
fixSteps.instruction: Monitor O2 sensor voltage at idle and revs.

fixSteps.title: Inspect exhaust
fixSteps.instruction: Look for leaks upstream of sensor.

fixSteps.title: Replace O2 sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new B1S1 sensor with proper anti-seize.

faq.a: Likely, yes, until this is fixed.

title: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 1, Sensor 3)
shortDescription: Oxygen sensor 3 on bank 1 reports high voltage.
fullDescription:
P0144 applies to vehicles with multiple O2 sensors per bank. The third sensor is reading higher than expected, usually pointing to a shorted sensor or rich exhaust condition.

Check for related rich running codes before replacing the sensor.

faq.a: Only on specific vehicles with extended exhaust sensors.

title: O2 Sensor Slow Response (Bank 1, Sensor 3)
shortDescription: The third O2 sensor on bank 1 responds too slowly.
fullDescription:
P0145 indicates the ECM has measured a slow transition time on B1S3. The sensor likely has contamination or is near end of life.

Long-term rich or oil-burning conditions accelerate sensor contamination.

fixSteps.title: Graph response
fixSteps.instruction: Observe sensor transitions on scan tool.

fixSteps.title: Check exhaust integrity
fixSteps.instruction: Find and fix leaks before sensor.

faq.q: How long do O2 sensors last?
faq.a: Typically 60k–100k miles.

title: O2 Sensor No Activity (Bank 1, Sensor 3)
shortDescription: The third oxygen sensor on bank 1 shows no activity.
fullDescription:
P0146 sets when the B1S3 sensor doesn't cycle as expected. Could be a failed sensor, broken wiring, or heater circuit problem.

Verify heater operation as part of diagnosis.

fixSteps.title: Verify heater
fixSteps.instruction: Check heater operation via scan tool.

faq.q: Difference between activity and response codes?
faq.a: Activity = no cycling; response = cycles too slowly.

title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit (Bank 1, Sensor 3)
shortDescription: Heater circuit fault on bank 1 sensor 3.
fullDescription:
P0147 indicates the ECM detected a fault in the heater circuit of B1S3. Heaters bring the sensor to operating temperature quickly; without it, closed-loop fuel control is delayed.

Check fuses and relays first.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new sensor if heater is failed.

faq.q: Can I ignore a heater code?
faq.a: Not long-term — it hurts emissions and fuel economy.

title: Injector Circuit Malfunction
shortDescription: A general fault has been detected in one or more fuel injector circuits.
fullDescription:
P0200 is a generic code indicating the ECM has detected an electrical issue with one or more fuel injector circuits. Specific cylinder codes (P0201–P0212) accompany it in many cases.

Causes include failed injectors, damaged wiring, or driver circuit faults in the ECM.
safetyImpact: Misfires, reduced power, potential catalytic damage.

fixSteps.title: Replace injector/wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Install replacement injector or repair wiring.

faq.q: Is P0200 always a bad injector?
faq.a: Not always — wiring or ECM driver issues can trigger it.

title: Injector Circuit Malfunction – Cylinder 1 (v2)
shortDescription: Alternate description — cylinder 1 injector circuit fault.
fullDescription:
P0201 (v2 description) indicates cylinder 1 injector has an electrical malfunction. Common causes include a failed injector coil, open or shorted wiring, or an ECM injector driver fault.

A bad cylinder 1 injector often pairs with a misfire code P0301.

fixSteps.title: Swap injectors
fixSteps.instruction: Swap cyl 1 and 2 injectors and re-test.

faq.q: How to confirm injector is faulty?
faq.a: Swap test between cylinders is the simplest method.

title: System Too Lean Bank 1 (v2)
shortDescription: Alternate description — bank 1 air-fuel ratio is too lean.
fullDescription:
P0171 (v2) sets when long-term fuel trim on bank 1 exceeds the positive threshold, indicating the engine is running leaner than the ECM can correct. Vacuum leaks and failing MAF sensors are top causes.

Unresolved lean conditions cause misfires and potential engine damage.

fixSteps.title: Smoke test
fixSteps.instruction: Locate vacuum leaks with smoke machine.

fixSteps.title: Check fuel pressure
fixSteps.instruction: Use a pressure gauge to verify fuel pressure.

faq.a: Vacuum leaks, especially on high-mileage vehicles.

title: System Too Rich Bank 1 (v2)
shortDescription: Alternate description — bank 1 is running too rich.
fullDescription:
P0172 (v2) is set when the bank 1 fuel trims show excessive fuel delivery. Leaking injectors, a failed MAF, or high fuel pressure are common causes.

Persistent rich running fouls spark plugs and damages catalysts.

fixSteps.title: Inspect injectors
fixSteps.instruction: Check for leaks or failed seals.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor/parts
fixSteps.instruction: Fix MAF, regulator, or injector as needed.

faq.q: Can bad oxygen sensor cause rich?
faq.a: Yes, if it reports falsely lean.

title: System Too Lean Bank 2 (v2)
shortDescription: Alternate description — bank 2 lean condition.
fullDescription:
P0174 (v2) sets when bank 2 fuel trims exceed positive threshold. Similar causes to P0171 apply — vacuum leaks, MAF issues, weak fuel delivery.

Often appears with P0171 if the cause is upstream (e.g., MAF or intake leaks).

fixSteps.title: Clean or replace MAF
fixSteps.instruction: Use MAF cleaner first; replace if needed.

faq.a: If only bank 2, check that side's components first.

title: System Too Rich Bank 2 (v2)
shortDescription: Alternate description — bank 2 rich condition.
fullDescription:
P0175 (v2) indicates bank 2 fuel trim is excessively negative. Leaking injectors, high fuel pressure, or a biased MAF can be the culprit.

Diagnose like P0172 but focus on the bank 2 side.

fixSteps.title: Replace leaking injector
fixSteps.instruction: Install new injector on affected cylinder.

faq.a: Suspect fuel pressure or MAF; single bank usually points to injectors.

title: Fuel Composition Sensor Circuit Malfunction (v2)
shortDescription: Alternate description — flex-fuel composition sensor fault.
fullDescription:
P0176 (v2) applies to flex-fuel vehicles where the ethanol/gasoline composition sensor reports an invalid signal. The ECM may default to a fixed fuel composition.

Fuel economy and drivability may suffer, particularly on E85.
safetyImpact: Low; drivability may degrade on flex fuels.

fixSteps.title: Check sensor data
fixSteps.instruction: Review ethanol % reading on scan tool.

faq.a: Yes; non-FFVs don't have this sensor.

title: Fuel Composition Sensor Range/Performance
shortDescription: Fuel composition sensor reading is implausible.
fullDescription:
P0177 indicates the composition sensor signal is within electrical range but changes implausibly or doesn't track fueling events. The injection pump or sensor may be suspect on diesel systems.

On FFVs, may also appear after mixing incorrect fuel.

fixSteps.title: Fuel quality check
fixSteps.instruction: Drain and refill with known fuel.

fixSteps.title: Test sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Verify output versus known ethanol level.

faq.a: Yes, poor-quality or mis-labeled fuel can trigger this.

title: System Voltage Malfunction
shortDescription: The ECM has detected a general system voltage fault.
fullDescription:
P0560 sets when the vehicle's system voltage is outside normal operating limits, either too low or fluctuating. This can stem from a weak battery, bad alternator, or poor electrical connections.

Many modules depend on stable voltage, so unrelated codes may follow.
safetyImpact: Potential stalling if voltage falls critically low.

fixSteps.title: Load test battery
fixSteps.instruction: Check battery with a load tester.

faq.a: Yes, prolonged low voltage reduces battery life.

title: System Voltage Unstable
shortDescription: System voltage is fluctuating beyond acceptable limits.
fullDescription:
P0561 is set when system voltage oscillates outside the expected range. A failing alternator or a loose ground can be responsible.

Unstable voltage can cause erratic module operation and many secondary codes.

fixSteps.title: Monitor voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Scan live data for voltage swings.

fixSteps.title: Test/replace alternator
fixSteps.instruction: Swap alternator if regulator is bad.

faq.a: A scan tool or scope that logs voltage over time.

title: System Voltage Low (v2)
shortDescription: Alternate description — low system voltage detected.
fullDescription:
P0562 (v2) is set when the ECM detects system voltage below the normal threshold for an extended period. Weak batteries, failing alternators, or parasitic drains are common causes.

Other modules may throw secondary codes due to under-voltage.

fixSteps.title: Replace component
fixSteps.instruction: Replace battery or alternator as needed.

faq.a: Temporarily yes, but diagnose the root cause.

title: System Voltage High (v2)
shortDescription: Alternate description — high system voltage detected.
fullDescription:
P0563 (v2) is set when system voltage exceeds the normal upper limit. An over-charging alternator or faulty voltage regulator is usually to blame.

High voltage can damage electronics and shorten bulb and battery life.
safetyImpact: Risk to modules and battery from overvoltage.

fixSteps.title: Measure charging voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Verify voltage at idle and high RPM.

faq.a: Short distances at most; overvoltage damages electronics.

title: Cruise Control Set Signal Malfunction
shortDescription: Cruise control SET switch signal has an electrical fault.
fullDescription:
P0570 indicates the ECM has detected an issue with the cruise control SET switch circuit. The switch may be stuck, wiring may be shorted, or a steering-wheel clock spring may be damaged.

Cruise control functionality is typically disabled until the fault is resolved.

faq.a: Yes, just without cruise control.

title: Cruise/Brake Switch A Circuit (v2)
shortDescription: Alternate description — cruise or brake switch A circuit fault.
fullDescription:
P0571 (v2) is set when the ECM detects an issue with the brake switch signal used by cruise control. When you press the brake, the cruise should disengage; an inconsistent signal sets this code.

Left unfixed, cruise will be disabled and braking indications may appear incorrect.
symptoms: Brake lights on constantly or erratic

faq.a: Usually yes — a cheap fix.

title: Cruise/Brake Switch A Low (v2)
shortDescription: Alternate description — brake switch A signal low.
fullDescription:
P0572 (v2) sets when the ECM detects the brake switch A signal is too low. Typically caused by a short to ground or failed switch.

Cruise is disabled as a safety measure.

faq.a: For safety if brake input is unreliable.

title: Cruise/Brake Switch A High (v2)
shortDescription: Alternate description — brake switch A signal high.
fullDescription:
P0573 (v2) is set when the brake switch A signal is too high — open circuit or short to voltage. Cruise control will be disabled.

Check the switch and wiring, then the brake-light fuse.

faq.a: A blown brake-light fuse produces an open-circuit signal.

title: Cruise Control System – Vehicle Speed Too High (v2)
shortDescription: Cruise system detects an implausibly high vehicle speed.
fullDescription:
P0574 (v2) is set when the cruise system receives a vehicle speed value above limits. The VSS or wheel speed input may be faulty.

Cruise control is disabled until fixed.

fixSteps.title: Scan all modules
fixSteps.instruction: Check ABS and body module codes.

faq.a: Yes — ABS modules often source wheel speed data.

title: Cruise Control Input Circuit
shortDescription: General fault with cruise control input circuit.
fullDescription:
P0575 is set when the ECM detects a fault with a generic cruise control input line. Could be any of the cruise buttons (SET, RESUME, COAST, ACCEL).

Cruise will be disabled.

fixSteps.title: Replace components
fixSteps.instruction: Install new switch cluster or clock spring.

faq.a: Often yes, with a multimeter and wiring diagrams.

title: Cruise Control Input Circuit Low
shortDescription: Cruise input circuit signal is below threshold.
fullDescription:
P0576 is set when the ECM detects a low-voltage condition on the cruise input line. Usually a short to ground or a stuck switch.

Cruise is disabled.

faq.a: Usually not for this code.

title: Cruise Control Input Circuit High
shortDescription: Cruise input circuit signal is above threshold.
fullDescription:
P0577 is set when the ECM detects high voltage on the cruise input line. An open circuit or short to voltage is likely.

Cruise is disabled.

faq.a: Yes, especially on older vehicles.

title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input Stuck
shortDescription: Cruise multi-function input signal is stuck.
fullDescription:
P0578 indicates that one of the cruise control buttons is stuck in the pressed position for an abnormally long time. Disables cruise to prevent runaway operation.

Check the switch cluster for mechanical sticking.

fixSteps.title: Clean or replace
fixSteps.instruction: Clean or install new switch cluster.

faq.a: Yes, sticky residue is a common cause.

title: Cruise Multi-Function Input Range/Performance
shortDescription: Cruise multi-function signal is out of range.
fullDescription:
P0579 indicates the ECM sees cruise switch signals outside expected values. Often caused by partial switch failure or wiring resistance.

Cruise will be disabled.

fixSteps.title: Read resistances
fixSteps.instruction: Measure each switch position vs spec.

faq.a: Not directly, but annoying and disables cruise.

title: Cruise Multi-Function Input Low
shortDescription: Cruise multi-function signal voltage is too low.
fullDescription:
P0580 is set when the multi-function cruise input is at a voltage below expected. Commonly a short to ground or bad switch.

Cruise will be disabled.

faq.a: Usually yes, with basic tools.

title: Cruise A/B Switch Correlation
shortDescription: Cruise control switches A and B disagree.
fullDescription:
P0585 is set when the ECM detects inconsistency between the A and B cruise switch signals. Steering-wheel mounted controls with redundant signals are common targets.

Cruise will be disabled.

fixSteps.title: Test both switches
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm A and B agree when pressed.

fixSteps.title: Replace components
fixSteps.instruction: Install new switch or clock spring.

faq.a: Redundancy for safety in steering-wheel controls.

title: Cruise Set/Resume Switch A Circuit
shortDescription: Cruise Set/Resume switch circuit A has a general fault.
fullDescription:
P0586 indicates a malfunction on the Set/Resume switch A circuit. Could be open wiring, short, or a stuck/failed button.

Cruise disabled.

faq.a: Possibly, if clock spring is involved.

title: Cruise Set/Resume Switch A Low
shortDescription: Set/Resume switch A voltage below threshold.
fullDescription: P0587 sets when the Set/Resume switch A signal is too low. Usually caused by a short to ground or stuck switch.

faq.a: Seen across many brands with steering-wheel cruise.

title: Cruise Set/Resume Switch A High
shortDescription: Set/Resume switch A voltage above threshold.
fullDescription: P0588 is set when the ECM sees high voltage on Set/Resume switch A — often an open circuit or short to voltage.

fixSteps.title: Inspect wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Check continuity and for shorts to voltage.

faq.q: Do I need to disable airbag?
faq.a: Yes, follow proper airbag safety procedures when removing steering wheel.

title: Cruise Set/Resume Switch B Circuit
shortDescription: Cruise Set/Resume switch circuit B has a general fault.
fullDescription: P0589 indicates the B circuit of the Set/Resume switch is malfunctioning. Could be a failed switch, bad clock spring, or wiring issue.

faq.a: For safety-critical cruise functions.

title: Cruise Set/Resume Switch B Stuck
shortDescription: Cruise Set/Resume switch B is stuck.
fullDescription: P0590 sets when Set/Resume switch B appears stuck in one position for too long. Mechanical binding or contamination are likely.

fixSteps.title: Inspect button
fixSteps.instruction: Check for sticky residue or debris.

fixSteps.title: Clean or replace
fixSteps.instruction: Clean contacts or replace switch cluster.

faq.a: Try cleaning first; replace if sticking persists.

title: Cruise Set/Resume Switch B Range/Performance
shortDescription: Cruise Set/Resume switch B signal out of expected range.
fullDescription: P0591 indicates switch B signal is within the electrical operating range but outside expected steps or positions. Often caused by resistor drift in the switch cluster.

faq.q: How long do these switches last?
faq.a: Typically 10+ years, but heavy use or contamination shortens life.
